body:
I think we don't need "filler" or "dramatically spoken" words without any technical meaning into requirement texts.

Started with words: properly, correctly, clearly, very

* properly; V5.2.1 [MODIFIED] Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is ~~properly~~ sanitized using a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature.
* properly; V5.4.4 [ADDED] Verify that dynamically allocated memory and resources are ~~properly~~ released, and that references or pointers to freed memory are removed or set to null to prevent dangling pointers and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
* correctly; V5.5.2 Verify that the application ~~correctly~~ restricts XML parsers to only use the _most restrictive configuration possible_ and to ensure that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled to prevent XML eXternal Entity (XXE) attacks.
  * "most restrictive configuration possible" requires some attention here as well
* properly; V6.3.3 [GRAMMAR, LEVEL L3 > L1] Verify that random number generation works ~~properly~~ under heavy system load, or that the system degrades gracefully.
* properly; V9.4.4 [ADDED] Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is supported and ~~properly~~ configured within the application’s TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), during TLS handshake processes.
* properly; V10.7.1 [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 1.11.3] Verify that only thread-safe types are used in multi-threaded contexts, or that non-thread-safe types are ~~properly~~ synchronized to prevent race conditions.
* clearly; V1.11.4 [ADDED] Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are ~~clearly~~ documented including both per-user and also globally across the application.
* very; V11.1.10 [ADDED] Verify that ~~very~~ high-value business logic flows are restricted with multi-user approval to prevent unauthorized or accidental actions. This could include but is not limited to large monetary transfers, contract approvals, access to critical nuclear facility operations, healthcare record modifications, access to classified information, or safety overrides in manufacturing.

"as secure as possible" - not actionable or verifiable
* V5.2.11 [ADDED] Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in Java Naming and Directory Interface (JNDI) queries and that JNDI is _configured as securely as possible_ to prevent JNDI injection attacks.
* V5.5.2 Verify that the application correctly restricts XML parsers to only use _the most restrictive configuration possible_ and to ensure that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled to prevent XML eXternal Entity (XXE) attacks.
